newsitem.title: USA: Sprint declines comment on Retevision.
newsitem.headline: Sprint declines comment on Retevision.

text.p: U.S. long distance firm Sprint Corp declined comment on a report it would join a group planning to buy a majority stake in Retevision, Spain's second largest telephone company after Telefonica de Espana.
A consortium of Banco Central Hispano, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG said it expects Sprint to join it in a bid for 60 percent of the Spanish state's stake in Retevision, which is for sale.
"We do not comment on speculation," a Sprint spokesman said.
However, the answer may soon be known. Declarations of interest in bidding are due on Monday.
If the government accepted the bidder, bids would be due by June 9.

Sprint is already allied with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom in Global One, a European-headquartered venture that acts as a one-stop telecommunications shop for multinational firms and a carrier of other telecom firms' traffic.

The report comes at a hectic time for Iberian telecommunications. Analysts are expecting Telefonica to join Concert, a global alliance between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp, and leave its Unisource alliance with AT&T Corp.
Portugal Telecom joined the Concert alliance on Monday.
Analysts say U.S. companies are jostling for position in the European market which is to be opened to full competition from the start of 1998 for several reasons.
One is the opportunities for growing local markets, and a second is filling in the geographical holes so they can offer services in any country in which business customers operate.

But the particular attraction for Iberian partners is to use the links and experience they have in marketing to Spanish or Portuguese speaking populations, which can be expanded in Latin America and the U.S itself. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
